claim_boundary: Output-informed descriptive cross-batch association for a simple declarative-history baseline on this fixed synthetic bank and model configuration.
interpretation_limits: The study is output-informed development on the same cases; it is not independent validation.
The declarative rewrite is a simple baseline and has no novelty claim.
Recommendation versus past-choice wording changes speech act and tokenization together.
Archived raw H=1 versus new declarative H=1 aliases surface form with execution batch; the repair effect is descriptive, not causal.
H=0 reuse avoids waste but aliases execution batch with H presence in the repaired factorial dataset.
Exact selection and lexical recurrence do not establish semantic correctness, internal copying, or absence of paraphrased historical influence.
Surface-style uptake is narrow prompt-template adherence, not broad Persona Fidelity.
Synthetic speakers and controlled choices do not support real-speaker or natural-dialogue claims.
Four synthetic persona clusters and twelve purposive cases support descriptive estimation only.
The shared model and partially verified third-party conversion lineage do not support cross-model generalization.
